The main takeaway from our work is that
, when regression imputation is used, sample correlation coefficients are not necessarily nearly unbiased and, in some cases, may not even be nearly unbiased.
, for the purpose of estimating population correlation coefficients, joint regression imputation should be preferred to marginal nonrandom regression.
, when the goal is to estimate a population correlation coefficient, the use of regression imputation should not be limited to imputing the values of the variable of interest.
